asked: a mouse with wings that can support its flight

phenotype.flight_structures_present_note: These were NOT asked for. They are in the blueprint because the word "flight" was recognised and the ontology records them as capable of it for this taxon; the structure that WAS asked for was refused. See conflicts[].substitution_warning.

by_cell.cell: CD24-positive, CD-133-positive, vimentin-positive proximal tubular cell
club-like cell of the urethral epithelium

genotype.note: marker gene products the Cell Ontology records for the chosen cell types. It is a sketch of what those cells express, not a genome and not a genotype anyone sequenced.

mesh.why: no surface mesh. anatomy-model/parametric is a teleost builder and Blender is absent on this machine; the 3D view is the ontology hierarchy, which is structure without shape.

what_it_taught: The request as posed cannot be built: Uberon asserts that a wing never occurs in Glires, so the blueprint of a winged mouse has no wing in it -- and TWO OTHER STRUCTURES IN ITS PLACE, promoted from the word "flight", which the first reading of this hierarchy missed entirely. The refusal is contradicted by the project inventory, which holds a gliding rodent inside that same clade. Separately, every harness tool refuses for want of a parameter set -- correctly, and by name.
question: Can a mouse grow wings that actually support its flight?
